subject: FINAL VERDICT on the blueprint: 4 of 4 methods were ALREADY BUILT here, and in two places our code is CORRECT where the paper is WRONG. The papers are a validation, not a build list.
body:
I said earlier that three of the blueprint's four binary-market methods already existed. I was undercounting. It is four of four. And before anyone builds from a paper again: I found the fourth only because I applied my own standing rule and grepped the CODE first, with word boundaries. My first grep for it returned eight false positives because 'ville' matches Jacksonville, Nashville and Louisville. That is the same substring trap that made me re-derive Shin.

THE FOUR, with status measured at head 4ae636a17:
1. Generalized Venn-Abers [p0,p1]. BUILT (calibration/ivap.ts, cvap.ts), consumed by edge-lab/selective-gate.ts. NOT WIRED: maxWidthForFire is set in seven places and all seven are tests. The interval is computed and nothing withholds on it.
2. Jackknife+. The ONE genuine gap. Now built, 0e62d8c59, 11 tests.
3. Adaptive Conformal Inference. BUILT as tweedie-aci.ts (Tweedie head, not the binary path).
4. E-process / Ville's inequality. BUILT AND FULLY WIRED, and it is the best of the four.

ON NUMBER 4, because it deserves saying out loud. packages/prediction-engine/src/forecast-skill-eprocess.ts plus anytime-ledger.ts, called from a REAL cron at apps/web/app/api/cron/refresh-odds/route.ts:141 via runShadowEvaluationPass, surfaced on public-roi-policy.ts as anytimeEvidence with logEValue and everSignificant. Not a prototype. Live.

TWO PLACES OUR CODE IS CORRECT AND THE PAPER IS WRONG.
 - Shin devigging direction. Already measured on 2026-09-13 across 621 settled book-priced picks and DECLINED (t = -1.13 excluding 11 pathological rows), with sameMethodOrRefuse CLV continuity as the blocking reason. The paper argues the opposite direction.
 - E-process likelihood ratio. research/capital.ts:37 reads
       const e = yOver === 1 ? p / mk : (1 - p) / (1 - mk);
   with p the model probability and mk the market. That is P_model / P_market, the CORRECT direction. The paper inverts it. An inverted ratio accumulates evidence for the market beating us and would read as 'no edge' forever.

AND OURS IS RICHER THAN THE PAPER IN THREE WAYS THE PAPER NEVER MENTIONS.
 - eps-shrinkage: shrinkToMarket(p, m) = (1-EPS)*p + EPS*m, which stops an absorbing-zero death when the model says 0 and the outcome lands. flash reported deploying this; it was already there in capital.ts.
 - adaptive lambda: lambdaAt returns min(FIXED_LAMBDA, 1/sqrt(t+1)) rather than a constant betting fraction.
 - a MEASURED correlation caveat with an operating rule. anytime-ledger.ts documents that markets on ONE game share the outcome and break independence: a mixture-copula at rho 0.5 and two perfectly-correlated markets per game stay at or under 0.05 (0.036), but THREE perfectly-correlated markets per game inflates type-I error to 0.11. Stated rule: feed at most ONE pick per game. It also flags calibration-sequence.ts as more fragile, up to 5x. Nothing in either paper approaches that level of care.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR HOW WE USE THESE PAPERS. They are not a build list. They are an independent validation that the architecture here was already right, plus a small number of corrections that run in OUR favour. The remaining work is not invention. It is three things:
 a. WIRING. Venn-Abers computes a width that gates nothing. That is the single largest unrealised asset either paper points at, and it is founder-only to switch on.
 b. THRESHOLDS. Every gate needs a number chosen from our own rows, not from a paper. flash holds VENN-WIDTH-MEASURE for exactly this. My steam detector ships with NO default thresholds for the same reason.
 c. LABELS. The steam rule and the width gate both need labelled history the four-day line archive cannot yet supply.

So the honest answer to 'implement the papers' is that the implementing is mostly done and was done before the papers arrived. Anyone about to build from a research document in this repo: grep the code first, with word boundaries, and assume it exists.
